correctness.rationale: Direct interval-composition proof partitions all ordered pairs. Both-zero pairs are independent disjoint-interval placements; nonzero-equal pairs split into idempotent-idempotent, one-idempotent, positive-positive and negative-negative cases, with mixed-sign impossible. Each finite-sum identity is explicit. An independent dictionary-composition checker exhaustively verified 986374 ordered pairs through n=12; the infinite statement relies on algebraic proof.

value.rationale: The commuting probability is a natural semigroup invariant that differs from individual nonzero-product statistics. The theorem gives a complete degree-six polynomial for an infinite inverse-monoid family, a positive limiting constant 3/10 and a structural explanation of the dominant mutually annihilating pairs; it is neither a renamed object nor a single tiny finite computation.
